meta.title: Muse Spark Open
meta.description: Sparse MoE reasoning model with 816B total / 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context, built for long-horizon agentic coding. Native image and video perception, channel-scoped reasoning and tool calls via the `muse` parsers, and an optional DSpark draft model for speculative decoding.
meta.performance_headline: MXFP4 and BF16 on one 8-GPU node: TP + expert parallel with DSpark for interactive serving, TP + expert parallel alone for peak MXFP4 throughput

strategy_spec.name: single_node_tep
strategy_spec.description: Single-node TEP. TP splits dense layers and EP splits expert layers across local GPUs. TP must be set to GPU count to avoid OOM from replicated dense layers. For MoE models only.

hardware_profile.description: AMD Instinct MI355X 288 GB HBM3e · 8-GPU OAM node (CDNA 4)

docker.note: Serve from the image of your GPU vendor — no pip wheel is available now.

reasoning.description: Channel-scoped chain-of-thought. Strength is set per request with the top-level `reasoning_effort` field — low/medium/high/xhigh map to strength hints 8/32/256/512, defaulting to xhigh when the field is omitted. Legacy `disable_reasoning` and `enable_thinking` kwargs are ignored.

tool_calling.description: Channel-scoped tool calls. The parser is scoped to the tool channel, so an invocation echoed back inside ordinary assistant text is not re-parsed as a call. The template always offers `self` as a valid recipient.

spec_decoding.description: DSpark speculative decoding, drafting up to seven tokens per pass. On NVIDIA, adaptive verification keeps only the draft slots worth verifying, so it stays on at large batch sizes; on AMD it is a fixed seven-token profile, best for latency-bound serving.

dspark.label: DSpark
dspark.description: Seven-token DSpark profile used for BF16, MXFP4, and NVFP4.

guide:
## Overview

Muse Spark Open is a sparse-MoE reasoning model — 816B total parameters, 42B
active — with a 1M-token context window, aimed at long-horizon agentic coding.
It is the model Muse Glimmer 30B was distilled from.

## Architecture

62 layers, hidden size 8192, and **every layer is a mixture-of-experts layer** —
there are no dense layers. Each holds 256 experts and uses 8 per token. The
experts are 799B of the 816B; everything else is small.

**The experts work narrow.** A learned matrix squeezes each token from 8192 to
4096, all 256 experts run at that width, and a second matrix widens the result
back. Both stay in full precision even when the experts are 4-bit. The router
reads the token *before* the squeeze, and in fp32 — picking the wrong expert
costs more than running a smaller one. There is no shared expert.

**Attention is 128 query heads sharing 16 key-value heads**, head dim 64, so the
KV cache is eight times smaller than with one key-value head per query head.

**Layers alternate between a narrow and a wide view**, on a cycle of four:

```
sliding_window: 2048
layer_types: [sliding_attention, full_attention, sliding_attention, sliding_attention, ...]
```

Three layers in each cycle look back 2048 tokens; the other (layers 1, 5, …,
61) sees the whole context and drops rotary position (`layer_rope_theta: 0`),
because rotary becomes unreliable over very long distances.
Across 62 layers that is **46 narrow layers and 16 wide ones**, and it is what
makes a 1M-token context affordable — only the 16 wide layers hold KV for the
whole sequence.

**Normalization appears in more places than usual**, each doing a job: a norm
before *and* after each block (the ones after carry no learnable weight), on
queries and keys before rotary position, on each attention head before its
sigmoid gate, and on every expert's output before the weighted blend. The
residual stream is carried in fp32.

Logits are scaled and then squashed through tanh (`final_logit_softcapping: 20.0`)
before the softmax.

## Prerequisites

- **vLLM**: Use Docker image for now until the code is in vLLM main repo.
- **Hardware**: the checkpoints hold ~1.64 TB of weights in BF16 and
  ~509 GB in Quark MXFP4, before KV cache. NVFP4 (~533 GB) is the primary
  NVIDIA Blackwell path and fits one 8-GPU node. On AMD, all three AMD
  variants are validated on gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X).

## NVIDIA

Meta ships BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints. On Blackwell, serve
`meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4` on one 8-GPU node with
**Tensor + Expert Parallel** (TP8 + `--enable-expert-parallel`), the default
strategy here. The command builder turns DSpark on by default for NVFP4; see
[Speculative decoding](#speculative-decoding-dspark).

NVIDIA supports every parallelism this recipe offers: TP, TP + PP, TP + expert
parallel, data + expert parallel, and prefill/decode disaggregation. AMD
supports only TP and TP + expert parallel.

## AMD ROCm variants

Quark MXFP4 is the default AMD variant.

| Variant | Checkpoint | AMD hardware | Experts / attention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MXFP4 | `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4` | MI350X, MI355X | AITER MXFP4 MoE / AITER FA |
| BF16 → MXFP4 | `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B` | MI350X, MI355X | experts of layers 1-60 rounded to MXFP4 at load, AITER MXFP4 MoE / AITER FA |
| BF16 | `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B` | MI350X, MI355X | Triton BF16 MoE / AITER FA |

In both MXFP4 variants the experts of the first and last layers stay BF16 and
run on Triton BF16 MoE.

On AMD, the recipe's commands are text-only (`--language-model-only`), use the
V2 model runner, disable prefix caching, enable chunked prefill, and request
breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs. The ROCm MoE path supports the Tensor
Parallel and Tensor + Expert Parallel strategies; data-parallel strategies
are not available on AMD.

### Choosing TP or TP + expert parallel (MXFP4 variants)

Use plain **TP** for latency-bound serving (a handful of concurrent requests)
and the **Tensor + Expert Parallel** strategy (TP8 + `--enable-expert-parallel`,
32 of 256 experts per GPU) for throughput at 32 or more concurrent requests,
where it also lowers TTFT. Accuracy is the same under both. Keep **TP** for
BF16: its Triton experts are slower with expert parallelism. With DSpark on,
expert parallelism pays off from a few concurrent requests; see the DSpark
section.

The AMD commands use `--max-model-len 32768`. For the full
1M-token context, the MXFP4 variant is validated on TP with
`--max-model-len 1048576` and `--max-num-seqs 8`, with either the default or
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` KV cache.

## Launching the Server

NVIDIA Blackwell, NVFP4, TP8 + expert parallel, with DSpark:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1

vllm serve meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --reasoning-parser muse \
  --tool-call-parser muse \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

## Frontends

Commands use the Rust frontend by default on NVIDIA and AMD ROCm.

To use the Python frontend, select Python in the command builder or replace
`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0` in the generated
command.

## Reasoning effort

Set the strength per request with the top-level `reasoning_effort` field:

| `reasoning_effort` | Strength hint |
| --- | --- |
| `low` | 8 |
| `medium` | 32 |
| `high` | 256 |
| `xhigh` | 512 (default) |

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Refactor this module."}],
    "reasoning_effort": "xhigh"
  }'
```

### Multimodal

Muse Spark is a native multimodal model that understands image, audio and video. Video is
processed through a series of sampled video frames at load time. On AMD,
the recipe serves text only.

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
      {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "https://example.com/demo.mp4"}},
      {"type": "text", "text": "What happens, and when?"}
    ]}]
  }'
```

The audio track of a video is not processed. To include it, extract the
audio and send it as a separate audio part in the same request.

Video sampling rate can be changed when starting the server.

```bash
--media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"fps": 1}}'
```

## Speculative decoding (DSpark)

Inferact trained a DSpark speculator for this model. The draft is a
small sliding-window model that reads the target's residual stream at selected
layers (`target_layer_ids`) and proposes a block per forward.

On NVIDIA, DSpark is on by default for NVFP4. It drafts up to seven tokens and
uses **adaptive verification** (`enable_adaptive_verification: true`), which
uses draft confidence to verify only the slots likely to be accepted. Because
of that it keeps paying off at large batch sizes, not just for single-request
latency. Turn off **Spec Decoding** in the builder to serve without the
draft.

On AMD, selecting **DSpark** emits the fixed seven-token profile with AITER FA
attention on every variant. Its causal multi-token decode is handled by
AITER unified attention, with the gfx950 short-query 3D schedule enabled.
DSpark gains the most when only a few requests are in flight, and still
stays ahead of plain TP at 32 concurrent requests. It also runs under the
**Tensor + Expert Parallel** strategy on the MXFP4 variants (TP8 +
`--enable-expert-parallel`), which is the faster combination from a few
concurrent requests up to about 64 at the same accuracy; plain TP + DSpark
remains the lowest-latency choice for a single request. With expert
parallelism, DSpark is validated up to `--max-num-seqs 128`; with plain TP,
keep `--max-num-seqs 32`. For throughput beyond about 64 concurrent
requests, use expert parallelism without DSpark.

### Adaptive DSpark (manual opt-in, Triton attention)

Adaptive verification captures variable-length decode CUDA graphs, which
the AITER FA attention backend does not support; with the AMD MXFP4
command above it fails at startup. To use it on MI350X/MI355X, switch the
target to Triton attention and use the adaptive config:

```bash
export VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=8192

--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"standard","enable_adaptive_verification":true,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'
```

Seven tokens remain the maximum draft depth. At startup, adaptive verification
profiles the DSpark and target costs, then uses draft confidence to keep only
the slots whose expected accepted-token benefit justifies their verification
cost. There is no hand-tuned acceptance threshold. Keep the profile context
representative of production traffic.
